# Inbound Fit Check

`sales.sit.inbound_fit_check` · v1.0.0 · **draft**

Owned by `sales.market_and_targeting.icp_definition`


> Interest has arrived from an account nobody has assessed, and the question before any other question is whether this account is one we should want. What distinguishes it from qualification, which fires on the same signals: qualification asks whether THIS purchase can happen — money, authority, timing — and it is the right question about a good-fit account. This situation asks the prior one, whether the account belongs in the pipeline at all, and it is answerable in minutes from public data where qualification takes a discovery call. Running them in the wrong order is how teams qualify their way carefully into accounts they should never have replied to.

> Bound to three of the twenty-six Layer 2 types, and all three are inbound-interest types rather than deal-state types — the binding is narrow on purpose, because a targeting capability that claims deal signals ends up second-guessing qualification. Nearly all the knowledge loaded here is currently blocked on firmographic enrichment: with no account.industry, account.employee_count or account.geography reaching the engine, the disqualifier list cannot fire and the fit reading is limited to what the first reply reveals, which arrives after the effort this situation exists to save.
